title: Python docstrings are not picked up as doc comments in read_symbol
description: DocComment (src/tools/research/read-symbol/doc-comment.ts) finds doc text by walking previousNamedSibling nodes of type comment directly above a definition. That matches JS/Go/Ruby convention (comment above the def), but Python real doc convention is a docstring: a string literal as the first statement inside the function or class body, not a preceding comment. python-tags.scm has no comment capture at all. Result: read_symbol docComment field comes back empty or wrong for Python symbols, even though the Python parser is otherwise closed. Needs a per language doc strategy: detect the body first expression_statement holding a string for Python instead of, or in addition to, the adjacent comment walk.

Wasms live in the app, never node_modules. Signature is the text before the body field, e.g. 'def fly(height: int):'. No changes to Definitions, SymbolTree or Outline.

title: Install config preview is a t template of config.json in its own file
description: The preview panel shows config.json as the installer will write it, with the field the current step edits drawn dark on gold. Today it is produced by searching the json text for a key (crow-config/highlight.ts, highlight/key-line.ts), which is the anti-pattern this replaces. The data is static in shape: two scalars, six permission lists, a providers list. The only dynamic parts are the values and which field is styled.
design: Three layers, strictly separated. DATA IN: ConfigPanelView#update builds { step, config: crowConfigFromInputs(values).crowConfig(), editedProvider: values.providers.length } from the inputs it already receives. DataStore and Subscriptions are not touched and hold nothing preview-shaped. TEMPLATE: a new module src/tui/install/views/steps/config-json/template.ts, one class, whose source reads like config.json. It is OpenTUI t-templates (StyledText) written at the file's own indentation and broken into sub-templates: the file shape, the permissions block, the providers list, one provider, plus field(step, text) which returns the text plain or dark-on-gold when step is current. A t hole only takes string, number, boolean or TextChunk (styled-text.d.ts lines 23 and 62), never a StyledText, so sub-templates nest by splicing .chunks. Lists print via JSON.stringify(items, null, 2) re-indented. Only the provider at editedProvider has styled holes. VIEW: ConfigJsonView#update(props) sets content from the template, height from its plain text, and scrolls once to the first styled chunk. Nothing else changes there. Delete highlight.ts, key-line.ts, their tests, and the HighlightJsonArguments and HighlightedJson types.
acceptance_criteria: tests/tui/install/views/steps/config-panel.test.ts passes UNCHANGED (every per-step span index). install-screen.test.ts and runner.test.ts unchanged and passing. A template unit test pins the default config text byte-for-byte to crowConfigJson() output and pins the providers block. git status shows nothing under data-store, subscriptions, crow-config/from-inputs. The template file is readable top to bottom as config.json.
notes: Three attempts were thrown out. Attempts 1 and 2: the agent loaded code-style, ran style-check, and extracted helpers and files to satisfy it (PermissionLines, ProviderLines, comma(), newline(), fieldStep(), ...). Attempt 3: a tagged-lines array computed on the DataStore as a configPreview signal with views drawing lines, then a t template inlined into the view class. Rules for the next attempt: do not load code-style or file-too-large, do not run style-check or pre-commit until the user asks, the user directs any split after seeing the draft. Do not put anything preview-shaped on the store. The template lives in its own file, not inside a view class. Show the code before claiming done.

title: Agent tab bar shows sessions and tab keys switch between them
description:
A tab bar shows each session with its number, a short title and whether it is running. Keys open a new session, close the active one, move to the next/previous session and jump to tab N.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Screen, Keys).

title: Agent holds several sessions, each running independently
description:
A SessionsStore holds a list of sessions and the active index, starting with one. It opens, closes and selects sessions. Keys and pastes go to the active session; Subscriptions effects render the active session; switching swaps input and history together. A session not in front keeps running its agent loop and writing its own history.

Settles whether sessions are persisted now or stay in memory.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Product, Store shape).

title: Agent loop runs model tool calls until a text reply
description:
A chat turn sends tool definitions with the history. When the reply has tool calls, each runs through the registry, call and result are appended to history and shown as tool entries, and the history is sent again; the turn ends on a text reply, a cancel, a model error, or a maximum number of tool rounds. Run state shows running tool while a tool runs.

See docs/agent-repl.md (The agent loop).

title: Escape cancels the session's running model request
description:
Escape cancels the session's running request. OpenAiRequest accepts an abort signal; a cancelled turn records a cancelled entry in history and returns the session to idle with the input usable.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Keys, The agent loop).

title: Agent chat turn sends history to the model and shows the reply
description:
Submitting input sends the system prompt plus the session's history to the session's model and appends the assistant's text reply to history. The run state shows waiting while the request is out. A model error appears in history as an error entry and the session stays usable.

Settles the system prompt open question: where it lives and what repository context it includes.

See docs/agent-repl.md (The agent loop).

title: Agent session holds one chosen model for the conversation
description:
A session holds one model for the whole conversation, chosen from configured providers with modelFindAllByFilters, and the status line shows it. Unlike Runner, the model does not change per request.

Settles the model choice open questions: default from config, picked per session in the UI, or both; and what happens when the model fails mid-conversation.

See docs/agent-repl.md (The agent loop, Open questions).

title: Tool registry exposes mutating file and git tools to the model
description:
The registry adds the mutating tools: edit, multi-edit, write, move, delete, delete directory, mkdir, git add and git commit.

Settles the approval open question: rely on path permissions alone, or ask the user per call (and whether that prompt blocks only its own session).

See docs/agent-repl.md (Tool registry, Open questions).

title: Agent status line shows the session model and run state
description:
A RunStore per session holds the run state (idle, waiting on model, running tool, failed). A status line under the input shows the session's model name (placeholder until a model is chosen) and its run state.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Screen).

title: Agent session history view shows entries by kind and scrolls
description:
A history view renders the session's entries by kind: user, assistant, tool call, tool result, error. It follows the newest entry and page up/page down scroll it. The view receives plain values from a Subscriptions effect, never a store.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Screen, Store shape).

title: Tool registry exposes read-only tools to the model
description:
A tool registry exposes the read-only tools (read, list, search, find, exists, GitReadOnly) to the model. For each tool: name, description and JSON-schema parameters for the request; validation of the model's JSON arguments into the operation's arguments; a run that returns the result, or the failure reason, as JSON text for the tool message. Path permissions are enforced by the existing operations.

The registry is product code for any repository and does not lean on this repository's dev tooling.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Tool registry).

title: Agent session input: type, edit and submit a message into history
description:
A SessionStore with an InputStore (InputText via src/tui/input-text.ts) and a HistoryStore. The DataStore holds exactly one session. Typing, paste, left/right/home/end, backspace/delete edit the input; shift-enter or a paste inserts a newline; enter appends the text to history as a user entry and clears the input. No model request yet. KeyboardListener routes keys to the session through DataStore#press/paste.

See docs/agent-repl.md (Store shape, Keys).

title: Model requests carry tool definitions, tool calls and tool results
description:
ModelMessages, now only { role, content }, grows the conversation shapes the agent loop needs: assistant messages with tool_calls, tool messages with tool_call_id, and tool definitions on the request. OpenAiRequest sends tools when given and returns tool calls from the reply. Existing callers (commit message, goals) keep working unchanged.

Settles the tool-call wire format open question (native OpenAI tools only, or a text-protocol default for models without tool calling).

See docs/agent-repl.md (The agent loop).

title: Every mutating git command is proven refused, against real git
description:
Every mutating git command is proven refused, against real git.

Refusal test over literal argument lists, each must fail with git never run:
- Subcommands that must never be enabled: add commit reset restore checkout switch merge rebase cherry-pick revert apply am pull fetch push clone init rm mv clean gc prune repack update-index update-ref symbolic-ref write-tree commit-tree hash-object mktag mktree bisect filter-branch replace pack-refs maintenance sparse-checkout lfs daemon instaweb web--browse send-email request-pull archive bundle, and difftool or mergetool, aliases, external git-foo.
- Known-bad forms: branch foo, tag v1, config user.name x, remote add, stash, reflog expire, log --output=f, diff --no-index, -c core.pager=x, -C .., --git-dir=.., abbreviated long flags (--out=f), pathspec :(top)x, HEAD:../../etc/passwd, -c alias.x=!sh.
- Path tests: show HEAD:allowed ok, show HEAD:denied refused, log -- denied refused, blame --contents denied -- allowed refused.

Real-git invariant (user decision: yes, and the repository must live in test support fixtures, not a temporary directory):
- Tracked seed files under tests/support/fixtures/tools/git/read-only/seed/. Git cannot track a nested .git, so a helper in tests/support/fixtures.ts (createGitFixtureRepository, clearGitFixtureRepository, same pattern as createSearchFixtureNodeModules) copies the seed into a gitignored tests/support/fixtures/tools/git/read-only/repo/ and runs real git init, add, commit with fixed GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* identity and dates and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null. Two commits, one untracked file, one modified file. Add the repo directory to .gitignore.
- Test uses mockApplicationData with cwd set to the fixture repo and no command override so real git runs. First assert git rev-parse --show-toplevel equals the fixture directory so a failed init can never run against the real checkout.
- For every allowed example from the subcommand stories, snapshot for-each-ref, status --porcelain=v2, the sorted .git file listing, and working-tree file contents before and after, and assert equal to a literal expected snapshot.

TDD: refusal list is a characterization test over final behavior (the only already-green test, each denial also has its own story test). Fixture helper red: undefined helper, stub makes an empty directory so git for-each-ref fails with 'not a git repository'.

title: Paths hidden in git arguments are checked against permissions
description:
Paths hidden in git arguments are checked against permissions.

Why: git accepts paths in many positions. Each must be extracted and checked with the same gitPathPermissions().allowsEvery call the existing git tools use (GitExec.requestedPaths feeding GitPathsGuard), so reads cannot escape the allowed directories.

Where paths appear, each needs a rule:
1. After the first bare --: pathspecs. Everything after it is a path, even if it starts with a dash.
2. Before -- as bare arguments: git treats an argument as a revision if it resolves, else a path. Do not depend on that. Treat every non-flag argument as a path as well as a revision and check it. Revisions like HEAD~3 or origin/main resolve under the repo root, so nothing legitimate is blocked.
3. rev:path object syntax (show, cat-file, diff, ls-tree, rev-parse): split on the first colon, the right side is also a path. Also the :n:path index form (starts with a colon, already rejected by the guard).
4. Path-valued flag values: --contents (blame), --ignore-revs-file, --pathspec-from-file, --file, -f, -O orderfile. Check them or do not allow the flag.
5. diff --no-index takes two arbitrary filesystem paths: not allowed.
6. Pathspec magic (:(top), :(glob), :(exclude), :!foo, :^foo, :/foo): any path starting with a colon is rejected, existing GitPathsGuard behavior. GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 (previous story) stops glob expansion.
7. Global options that retarget (-C, --git-dir, --work-tree) are already refused, which stops escape to other repos or submodules. Git always runs with cwd at the repo root.

Resolution: reuse the existing permission resolver, which handles .. and symlinks. Check all paths, one denied path fails the whole command, message names every denied path: 'path not allowed: ../a, ../b'. Git is not run on denial. If permissions ever narrow below the repo root, commands without explicit paths (log -p, diff, show, grep) would need a pathspec injected or denied, noted as a future concern since git permission is currently the repo root.

TDD cycles: paths after --, bare arguments before --, rev:path (abc123:src/a.ts yields both, abc123:../x denied), path-valued flag (--contents=notes.txt allowed, --contents=../x denied), pathspec magic denied, several denied paths all named.

title: Unsupported git subcommands, flags and global options are refused
description:
Unsupported git subcommands, flags and global options are refused.

Why: safety comes from allowing known subcommands and flags, never from blocking known-bad ones. Git has hundreds of flags and abbreviates long options (--out means --output), so a blocklist is bypassable. No subcommand is enabled at the end of this story, so nothing runs yet.

Work: GitReadOnly operation extending GitExec, arguments { args: string[] }, result { stdout: string } (GitOutput in src/tools/types.ts). Logger prefix 'Git read only: '.

Rules:
- Argument list starts with the subcommand. Global options are refused outright: -C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --exec-path, --namespace, --super-prefix (they retarget git or set config such as core.pager, core.fsmonitor, diff.external, alias.x=!cmd, core.sshCommand, all of which execute code). Message: 'subcommand not allowed: -C'.
- Unknown subcommands refused (this also blocks aliases and external git-foo binaries).
- Some subcommands are allowed only in a particular form: first positional gates it (stash list yes, stash pop no, stash bare no). Message: 'subcommand not allowed: stash pop'.
- A flag is accepted only when it is an exact allowed spelling. No abbreviations (--one for --oneline), no clustered short flags (-nw). Long valued flags only as --name=value. Short valued flags as -n 5 or -n5. Valued flags validated (number flags reject 'x': 'flag value not a number: -n x').
- Flags that write or execute even on read subcommands, which tests must show are refused: --output=<file> and -o (diff, log, show, format-patch write files), --ext-diff, -O<orderfile>, --open-files-in-pager (grep), --exec=<cmd>, --upload-pack, --receive-pack, --lost-found (fsck), --no-index, --batch, --batch-command (cat-file), --edit and -e, --help (spawns man or a pager), --git-dir, --work-tree, -C, --exec-path, --namespace, -c key=value.
- Failure messages name every offending flag, not a count: 'flag not allowed: --output=f, --exec=x'.

TDD cycles (tests configure the enabled subcommands inline): nothing enabled denies log with zero command calls, enabled subcommand runs and returns stdout (failure returns empty stdout), allowed flag passes, unknown flag, abbreviation, valued flag forms, global options, form gating, all offenders named.

title: Git runs in a locked-down environment
description:
Git runs in a locked-down environment.

Why: a repo's own config, attributes and the parent process environment can make a read-only git command run code (pagers, editors, external diff, fsmonitor, hooks, askpass) or take index locks. Run every read-only git call with a scrubbed environment and fixed config overrides supplied by the tool, never by the caller.

Work:
- CommandOptions gets optional env. Bun.spawn receives it as given (replaces, does not merge with process.env). Existing tools pass no env and are unchanged.
- Locked-down environment sets: GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 (status and diff must not take index.lock or refresh the index), GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_PAGER=cat, PAGER=cat, GIT_EDITOR=: , EDITOR=: , GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 (a surviving * is not expanded to reach forbidden paths).
- Removes when present: GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES (retargeting), GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS.
- Fixed argument prefix before the subcommand: --no-pager -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.pager=cat -c diff.external= -c protocol.allow=never -c core.untrackedCache=false.
- Where a subcommand supports them, pass --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv (repo .gitattributes can name diff and filter drivers whose commands come from .git/config).

Residual risk: textconv or filter drivers in an untrusted repo's .git/config. Overrides above close the known ones. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null is POSIX only, other platforms out of scope. GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 means status may show stale stat info, accepted.

TDD: characterize runtimeExec without env (already green), then red/green per behavior: env replaces child env (printenv returns the value), parent variables do not leak when env is given, the locked-down environment equals the literal expected object, the argument prefix equals the literal expected list. Run dev/test tests/tools/git to prove existing tools unchanged.

title: OpenTUI runner
description: New runner in the parallel OpenTUI directory: createCliRenderer with injected stdin/stdout/stderr, exitOnCtrlC false and exitSignals empty so the runner owns SIGINT/SIGTERM via runtime.addSignalListener, renderer.destroy() and await renderer.closed on every path, ReplStatus result. notes: Spike findings: createRoot comes from @opentui/react, usage createRoot(renderer).render(element). createCliRenderer is async and accepts stdin, stdout, width, height, exitOnCtrlC, exitSignals, screenMode (alternate-screen, main-screen, split-footer), useKittyKeyboard, bufferedOutput, onDestroy and more. It has no stderr option, so ReplIo.stderr cannot be forwarded and the runner must write errors itself. exitOnCtrlC false plus exitSignals empty kept handlers off the process. Ink mapping: useApp().exit becomes renderer.destroy() then await renderer.closed, useStdin raw mode support has no equivalent so guard in the runner, alternateScreen true is the default screenMode. The runner must stay open until exit: destroying right after startup leaked the terminal replies to the capability queries into the shell as garbage text on a real terminal and drew nothing. Await renderer.idle() after render, then wait for the exit signal, then destroy and await closed. Verified on a real terminal: a box with text draws and a keypress exits cleanly. Without a TTY, PassThrough streams with isTTY true, setRawMode, columns and rows are accepted. Output then shows ESC[?1049h on start and ESC[?1049l on teardown, but the first frame is never painted because nothing answers the capability queries, so assert lifecycle sequences there and use testRender for frames.

title: Agent can list branches, tags, remotes, config, stashes, worktrees and reflog
description:
Agent can list branches, tags, remotes, config, stashes, worktrees and reflog.

Only listing forms. Safety depends on the subcommand plus its first argument, not on the subcommand alone.

- branch: bare, -a, -r, -v, --list, --show-current, --contains, --merged. Refused: -d -D -m -M -c -C -f --set-upstream-to --unset-upstream --edit-description, and any bare argument (branch foo creates a branch).
- tag: -l, --list, -n, --points-at, --contains. Refused: -d -a -s -f -u -m, and any bare argument (tag v1 creates a tag).
- remote: bare, -v, get-url. show hits the network unless -n, so not included. Refused: add remove rename set-url set-head prune update.
- config: --get, --get-all, --get-regexp, --list, -l. Refused: any set, unset, edit, --add, --replace-all, --rename-section, --remove-section, -e, and bare config key value (writes).
- stash list only. Refused: push pop drop apply clear and bare stash.
- worktree list only. Refused: add remove move prune lock unlock repair.
- reflog show (or bare). Refused: expire, delete.
- Excluded: submodule status, notes list/show, var, version, help (help may spawn a pager or browser) can be follow-ups.

First TDD cycle: forms that take no arguments refuse any extra argument ('argument not allowed: foo'), red against the earlier behavior that accepted positionals. Then allow and deny cycles per subcommand with the refusals above as the deny examples.
